note: Chapter XVII fill shots (Ian, 16 Nov): exteriors, far angles, window views, down the hall — general shapes to rest the eye while the story is told.
style: A painting of 1893 in the manner of the reference: academic realism, luminous daylight or dusk, plein air, rich colour and atmosphere, a wide establishing view. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Exterior, Piccadilly, London, a grey September morning in 1893: the front of a grand hotel, hansom cabs and a four-wheeler at the kerb, gas lamps, wet pavement, tall stone buildings receding into haze. Any people are small, distant figures with no detail in their faces.

Exterior, Paddington Station, London, 1893: the great iron-and-glass train shed seen from the end of the platform, a steam train arriving under the arched roof, plumes of steam in shafts of daylight, crowds on the platform. Any people are small, distant figures with no detail in their faces.

Exterior, the asylum at Purfleet in the Essex countryside, 1893, late afternoon: a large plain Georgian building behind iron gates and a high wall, a gravel drive, elms, a cab drawing up at the gates; the Thames marshes flat and grey beyond. Any people are small, distant figures with no detail in their faces.

Exterior at dusk: seen from the asylum grounds across a high old stone wall, the neighbouring house Carfax: a huge, gloomy, half-ruined old mansion of heavy stone with few high barred windows, a squat old chapel joined to it, dark trees, a weedy pond, ravens.

Exterior, Whitby, Yorkshire, a clear blue September day in 1893: the harbour and river mouth seen from the West Cliff, red-roofed houses tumbling down both sides, fishing boats and a collier at the quay, the ruined abbey and the church on the East Cliff against the sky, the two piers running out to sea.

Exterior, King's Cross Station, London, early morning in 1893: the plain brick front with its two great arched windows and clock tower, carts and drays in the forecourt, horse-drawn omnibuses, a pale sun in smoky air. Any people are small, distant figures with no detail in their faces.

Exterior, a busy London street in 1893: a large carrier's depot with wide open gates, horse-drawn vans with painted sides loading crates, carters in aprons, cobbles, brick warehouses, smoke and sunlight. Any people are small, distant figures with no detail in their faces.

Exterior at dusk: the old chapel of Carfax seen across an overgrown yard, its stone walls stained and crumbling, tall pointed windows dark, a heavy oak door studded with iron, nettles and ivy, a pale evening sky.

Exterior, the asylum at Purfleet in the evening, 1893: a hansom cab has stopped at the lit doorway, two tall figures stepping down, golden lamplight from the windows onto the gravel, the sky deep blue above dark elms. Any people are small, distant figures with no detail in their faces.

Exterior, the Thames marshes near Purfleet on a still autumn afternoon, 1893: flat reed beds, a tidal creek, sailing barges with brown sails on the wide river, the distant asylum roofs among trees, a soft hazy sky.
